title: Tip to prevent food overconsumption and fat gain
summary: NH shares a simple maintenance tip for people who eat by feel rather than counting calories: eat until satiated, not full, pausing for 30 seconds to a couple of minutes and saving leftovers. Appetite naturally varies so intake self-balances across days, as long as protein is met. He recommends cutting back on the post-workout evening meal rather than the pre-workout meal, and notes it isn't suited for cutting, refeeds or people with disordered appetites.

claims.claim: This method is for people who don't count calories and eat by feel; counting calories makes it useless, and it only works if you eat for sustenance, aren't food-addicted and your appetite is disciplined.
To stay at maintenance, eat until satiated rather than full; most people keep eating after hunger is gone due to momentum and being raised to finish their plate.
Pause about 30 seconds mid-meal; if you're no longer hungry, your body has had enough, so pack the rest away for later.
On days your body needs more you'll stay hungry and finish; on low-appetite days you eat less, so intake self-balances across days at maintenance or slight surplus.
This approach is terrible for cutting because your body constantly asks for calories in a deficit.
Smaller meals are fine as long as you get your protein in; you won't lose muscle or hurt performance.
He trains, eats and then goes to bed; that last post-workout meal is the best one to cut back on, while reducing the pre-workout meal hurts training energy.
If you wake up not very hungry, you ate what you needed the night before.
He admits he gets greedy with food and often serves twice what he needs, which would push him into a bigger surplus than wanted; the method also saves money.
Don't apply this on refeed, carb-up or cheat days where you want calories to spike.
The method suits instinctive eaters with neither low nor high appetite.
